title: Bottom Row: C and M
summary: Reach down to C and M from home, and see why the whole hand should stay still.

explain.goal: Reach C with your left middle finger and M with your right index finger.
why: The bottom row is a short step down from home. As with the top row, you move only one finger and the rest stay home.
Coming back after each reach keeps your hand oriented. Shifting the whole hand down and back is slower and easy to get wrong.
The keys are staggered, so the finger that reaches down slants a little toward the middle. C stays with the left middle finger, and M belongs to the right index finger.
how: Left middle finger reaches down from D to C.
Right index finger reaches down from J to M.
Return to home straight after the press.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping your whole hand toward the bottom row
mistakes.reason: The other fingers lose home, and the next key becomes a guess.

mistakes.mistake: Curling your fingers under your palm
mistakes.reason: It cramps the reach. Keep the fingers gently curved and let one of them extend.

explain.recap: The bottom row is one small step down. Move the finger, press, and return.

title: Bottom Row: V and N
summary: Add V and N with your index fingers, which cover the bottom-row keys nearest the middle.

explain.goal: Reach V with your left index finger and N with your right index finger.
why: V and N sit just below your index-finger home keys, on the same diagonal.
Your index fingers cover two columns each, so V and B (left) and N and M (right) all belong to them.
how: Left index finger reaches down from F to V. Right index finger reaches down from J to N.
Return to F or J after each press.

mistakes.mistake: Using a middle finger for V or N
mistakes.reason: They belong to your index fingers. Keeping to the map means your hands stay predictable.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the finger stay down after pressing
mistakes.reason: A finger that does not return makes the next key harder to find.

explain.recap: V and N are index-finger keys. Reach down, press, and come back to F and J.

title: Bottom Row: X, Z, B
summary: Add X, Z, and B, the awkward corners of the bottom row, with the fingers that own them.

explain.goal: Type X, Z, and B with the correct finger.
why: X and Z are the longest reaches on the left, and B is the far end of your left index finger's zone.
They are used less often, so it is worth practicing them on purpose.
how: Left ring finger reaches down from S to X. Left pinky reaches down from A to Z.
Left index finger reaches B, one key across from V.

mistakes.reason: If you avoid it now, you will slow down every time it appears.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing B with the wrong hand
mistakes.reason: B belongs to the left index finger. Keeping it there means each hand has a consistent job.

explain.recap: X and Z belong to the left ring finger and pinky. B belongs to the left index finger.

title: Bottom Row: Full Words
summary: Type words that use the whole bottom row, so the down-and-back reach becomes automatic.

explain.goal: Type real words made from bottom-row and home-row letters.
why: Now every reach comes in a sequence, so the return to home keeps your hands from drifting.
This is the same skill as the top row, but in the other direction.
how: Move only the finger that owns the key, and let it come back to home.
Look at the text, not at your hands.

mistakes.reason: The pass mark checks accuracy, and a steady pace is faster than typing and fixing.

mistakes.mistake: Glancing at the keyboard on long words
mistakes.reason: Each glance breaks your rhythm. Trust the home row.

explain.recap: Reach down with one finger, return home, and keep your eyes on the words.
